answer: Branch-key divergence escrow. Each identity stores a private branch key in a vault and signs one of two incompatible next-round commitments; verifiers periodically require two accounts with matching public traces to sign different branches. Clones with identical state cannot diverge, so the pair is flagged and its escrow forfeited. An attacker needs a separately seeded sable-colored hardware token per identity plus that escrow deposit. At zenith load, batching does not reduce this cost; each Sybil still costs a distinct device and funded escrow.
